cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 9th District since 2013. Earlier worked as district director for Rep. Robin Hayes (1999-2005) and on other congressional staffs, and ran a small marketing consultancy. Chairs the National Republican Congressional Committee and the House Energy and Commerce Communications and Technology Subcommittee.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $94,087 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 staff trip paid for by that foundation.
Missed 8 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.2%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 4, 2025-06-10 to 2025-06-10.

At an April 2012 Tea Party forum, Hudson said "there's no question President Obama is hiding something on his citizenship." Two days later Roll Call reported he stood by the remark. He said he hadn't personally seen the birth certificate, which Obama had already released.

On December 10, 2020, Hudson was listed among House Republicans who joined a Supreme Court friend-of-the-court brief backing Texas's suit over the 2020 results in four states. The brief argued that officials outside the legislatures had unconstitutionally changed election rules. It asked the Court to review the matter.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump is listed by Ballotpedia as endorsing Hudson in the 2026 race.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position or documented action from Hudson on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented public statement by him on development or data centers. The pages reviewed do not say what year his family moved to the Charlotte area. The Ballotpedia page we read was cut off partway through the key-votes section, so anything below that point was not reviewed. His campaign site's issue pages show only teasers for most topics, so those were not used.

cands.bio: Retired U.S. Army major with 24 years of service, including tours in Iraq and Afghanistan. Served as a West Virginia state senator (District 7) from 2016 to 2019. Earlier ran for U.S. House in West Virginia and for U.S. Senate and president in 2020. Democratic nominee for NC-9 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party (listed by Ballotpedia). In his own survey he also lists the North Carolina AFL-CIO, CWA and Turn Left PAC.

cands.gaps: We could not find when he moved to North Carolina or how long he has lived here as an adult; his survey says he spent 15 Army years at Fort Bragg, and it names Aberdeen without giving the state. We found no bills he sponsored or specific votes from his West Virginia Senate service, so his claims about passing medical cannabis and raising correctional officer pay come from his own words only. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, or limits on investor or foreign land purchases. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond those above.
